content.caption: Accuracy versus median (p50) and tail (p95) latency for the Base, Base + Reranker and Memory-R1 (GRPO) inference pipelines, shown separately for F1, BLEU-1 (B1) and LLM-judge (J) scores.
content.description: Line-and-marker chart in three side-by-side panels titled 'F1 (↑)', 'B1 (↑)' and 'J (↑)'. The up arrows mean higher is better. Per the page, B1 is BLEU-1 and J is the LLM-as-a-Judge score. The left panel carries the shared y-axis label 'Accuracy (%)'. Each panel has its own y-range: F1 ticks run 30–44 in steps of 2, B1 ticks run 22–38 in steps of 2, and J ticks run 45.0–62.5 in steps of 2.5. Each x-axis is 'Latency (s)' on a log scale where only the 10^0 (1 s) tick is labelled, with light grid lines. A legend across the top maps colours: blue = Base, orange = Base + Reranker, green = Memory-R1 (GRPO). A key at the top right shows a black filled circle = p50 (median latency) and a black triangle = p95 (tail latency). In every panel, each pipeline is a horizontal line joining its p50 circle (left end) to its p95 triangle (right end) at one accuracy level, so line length shows the median-to-tail latency spread. No values are printed. All numbers below are estimated read-offs, and the latencies are rough because only 10^0 is labelled. Latency positions are the same in all three panels: Memory-R1 (GRPO) runs from ≈0.3 s (p50) to ≈0.6 s (p95) at the left edge. Base runs from ≈1.1 s (p50, near the 10^0 tick) to ≈2.8 s (p95) and is the longest line. Base + Reranker runs from ≈3.5 s to ≈4.6 s, a short segment at the far right. Accuracies: F1 – Memory-R1 ≈45.0, Base + Reranker ≈32.7, Base ≈30.4. B1 – Memory-R1 ≈37.5, Base + Reranker ≈24.8, Base ≈22.2. J – Memory-R1 ≈62.7, Base + Reranker ≈60.0, Base ≈45.7. Comparisons: in every panel Memory-R1 (GRPO) sits alone in the top-left corner, combining the highest accuracy with the lowest median and tail latency; its whole range is below 1 s. Base is the least accurate pipeline and has the widest p50–p95 spread. Adding the reranker lifts accuracy only slightly over Base for F1 (+≈2.3) and B1 (+≈2.6), but strongly for J (+≈14, close to Memory-R1). At the same time it moves both latency percentiles furthest right, to the highest values of several seconds; its p50 lies beyond even Base's p95.
